text:
Noelle: Quick sync on a compact legend pattern I'm prototyping. Goals: keep chart width for data, make series mapping discoverable, and ensure keyboard/screenreader friendliness. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-legend-proto

Priya: Sounds good. Accessibility red flags: don't hide series names entirely. If we show abbrevs only, each swatch needs an aria-label with the full name. The expand control must be a semantic button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

Felix: Engineering notes: popovers can get clipped in embedded dashboards. Prefer an inline expandable region that grows below the small-panel charts. We can reuse the Drawer component that works well in narrow containers.

Dana: Visual idea: inline row of swatches + 3-char abbrev (e.g., "Auth", "DB") with a trailing "Show full key" chevron. Clicking opens a small inline drawer with full list + search. On very tiny tiles, drawer becomes stacked legend under the chart.

Priya: Keyboard & SR details:
- Expand button: <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="series-key-list" aria-label="Show series key, 7 series">Show key</button>
- When opened: move focus into <ul id="series-key-list" role="listbox">; Arrow keys navigate; Space toggles visibility.
- Provide aria-live polite region for state changes: "Series X hidden" and for unit/outlier changes. Debounce 250ms and coalesce messages.

Noelle: Good. Units: should axis show "Errors per minute" or "err/min"? Proposal: full label under axis + compact tick values. Tooltips on ticks show the long wording. Also add aria-labels on ticks e.g., visual "1.2K" -> SR "1,200 errors per minute".

Felix: I'll add a formatNumberAccessible util for that. Also note rapid toggles can spam the aria-live region; we'll group changes and emit summaries like "2 series visible, 5 hidden" when appropriate.

Dana: Outlier handling: product wants trends preserved. My mock pins a subtle "+n" badge top-right when points lie outside current y-scale. Badge is a focusable button: aria-label "Three points excluded from scale. Press Enter to include." Clicking expands the axis to include them.

Priya: Microcopy suggestions:
- Expand closed: "Show series key, 7 series"
- Expand opened: "Hide series key"
- Outlier badge: "{n} points outside visible range. Press Enter to include in scale."
- Unit change announcement: "Axis units updated to thousands."

Noelle: Smoothing control: analytics show low per-chart usage. Move smoothing into overflow (three-dot) menu under "Line options" with help text: "Smooth lines to show trend; may hide peaks." Default OFF for perf charts.

Felix: Implementation trade-offs:
- Drawer + inline fallback increases DOM but avoids clipping issues.
- Roving tabindex util exists so Arrow key nav is straightforward.
- formatNumberAccessible will need a mapping of unit strings per chart type.

Dana: Visual tweaks: increase thin-line min stroke to 1.5px or use higher-contrast token. Add caret on the expand control and a 44px hit area. In the drawer, show search when series >8.

ux-bot: Reminder: staging deploy tonight 23:00-23:30 UTC; tests may be impacted.

Noelle: Decision summary for sign-off:
1) Inline compact key (swatch + 2-4 char abbrev) with a semantic expand button (aria-expanded + aria-controls).
2) Expand reveals inline drawer with full names + search; stacked fallback under chart for tiny panels.
3) Provide aria-labels for abbrevs and accessible tick labels via formatNumberAccessible.
4) Outliers shown as de-emphasized markers with a focusable "+n" badge to include them in scale; badge hidden when n=0.
5) Move smoothing to overflow menu; default off for perf dashboards.

Priya: I'll post the exact ARIA strings and a short QA checklist later today. Felix: can you prototype the drawer + formatNumberAccessible this sprint?

Felix: Yep, I'll spike it and drop a short screen recording here.

Noelle: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the prototype and copy draft. :raised_hands:
